title: Rapid integration pilot session flow and slide notes
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a practical script and slide map for a 3-hour customer pilot session aimed at validating integration patterns, measuring latency/cost tradeoffs, and establishing next-step commitments for a small cohort customer. Target audience: product engineers, platform owners, and solutions/infra liaisons from the customer side. Primary goals: (1) confirm API integration feasibility within customer network constraints, (2) demonstrate latency and cost knobs (batching, caching, model variant routing), (3) gather perf metrics on representative traffic, (4) align on a 30-day pilot success definition.

Pre-reqs (prior to session):
- Customer provides a representative prompt set or sample traffic (10–50 requests) and a test dataset for embeddings/tasks.
- Engineering access: API key scoped for pilot, temporary VPC peering info (if private), or FW rules for hosted endpoint.
- Local laptop with curl/HTTPie, Python (3.9+) and the Redwood SDK installed.
- Team roster with a single technical owner and a business sponsor.

Session timing (3 hours):
- 0:00–0:10 — Welcome & success criteria (lead: Jordan)
  - Quick intros, session objectives, and confirm top 3 success metrics (latency P95 target, cost per 1k tokens, functional correctness rate).
- 0:10–0:25 — Customer context and constraints (lead: customer eng)
  - Customer explains architecture, traffic shape, data residency requirements, and security constraints.
- 0:25–0:45 — Architecture walkthrough & integration options (lead: Marcus)
  - Show hosted vs dedicated vs private. Discuss routing/fallback policies and typical tradeoffs.
- 0:45–1:10 — Live integration demo — hello-world call and auth patterns (lead: Priya)
  - Step-by-step: SDK init, sample prompt, response streaming on, with fallback toggled. Provide curl and Python examples.
- 1:10–1:40 — Hands-on: customer runs sample traffic (lead: customer tech, with SE support)
  - Run provided prompts, capture latency, error rates, and token counts. SEs observe and collect logs.
- 1:40–1:55 — Break
- 1:55–2:25 — Performance tuning lab (lead: Marcus)
  - Toggle batch size, enable prefix caching, try a smaller quantized model variant; record P50/P95 token latency and cost delta.
- 2:25–2:50 — Failure modes & resilience (lead: Sofia)
  - Simulate region outage or capacity throttling, show automatic fallback and graceful degradation behavior. Validate request routing rules and canary rollback.
- 2:50–3:00 — Wrap-up, actions, and pilot next-steps (lead: Jordan)
  - Confirm owner for pilot instrumentation, dates for follow-up checkpoint, and acceptance criteria.

Slide map (15 slides recommended):
1. Title & logistics — session agenda and outcomes
2. Pilot objectives & success metrics — measurable KPIs
3. Customer context snapshot — traffic shape & constraints (customer-provided)
4. Redwood integration options — hosted vs dedicated vs private (decision table)
5. Security & compliance checklist — KMS, audit logs, VPC notes
6. Authentication & request flow — example calls and token flows
7. Live demo notes — what attendees will see and what to watch for
8. Observability & cost view — Console screenshots and token breakdown expected
9. Experiment matrix — variables to change in lab (batch, cache, model)
10. Lab step-by-step — commands and expected outputs
11. Metrics capture plan — how we collect latency, tokens, errors (tools & endpoints)
12. Resilience scenarios — failure modes and expected behaviors
13. Pilot timeline & responsibilities — 30-day runbook summary
14. Success criteria checklist — pass/fail gates for go/no-go
15. Next steps & open questions — owners and dates

Facilitation notes and cues (concise):
- Kickoff: ask the customer to name their top 3 concerns aloud and pin them in chat. Revisit these at the end.
- Live demo: keep one pre-seeded prompt to guarantee a deterministic output if network flakiness occurs; fall back to recorded transcript if needed.
- Hands-on lab: have one SE per customer table (or breakout room). Provide a single canonical script file and numbered checkpoints to reduce cognitive load.
- Tuning lab: capture three runs for each configuration (baseline, +batching, +caching) and compute median P95 to reduce noise.
- Failure simulation: warn attendees before injecting failure and have a manual rollback ready (toggle rule in control plane).

Data capture & artifact checklist (what SEs must produce during session):
- Raw logs: request ID list, token counts, per-request latency (ms), error traces.
- Console snapshots: per-route latency graphs and token cost panel.
- Short debrief note: 10–15 bullet summary including top 3 risks and recommended mitigations.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Session lead (Jordan): overall flow, success criteria alignment, follow-ups.
- Demo owner (Priya): authentication, sample calls, SDK examples.
- Perf owner (Marcus): lab setup, metrics capture, and tuning recommendations.
- Resilience owner (Sofia): failure scenarios and fallback validation.
- Customer tech owner: run hands-on steps and validate behavior in their environment.

Common pitfalls & troubleshooting quick-reference:
- Auth errors: check token scope and expiry; ask customer to paste sanitized 401 logs.
- High P95 but low P50: likely cold KV-cache or batch misconfiguration — increase prefix cache or lower batch window.
- Unexpected truncation: verify model max tokens + prompt length; use streaming to confirm incremental output.
- Network timeouts: confirm firewall or NAT idle timeout is not closing long-lived streams.

Post-session deliverables (within 3 business days):
- Instrumentation bundle from SEs (logs + metric screenshots).
- Short pilot runbook with agreed measurement plan and ownership.
- Follow-up meeting scheduled (day 7 checkpoint) to review first-week telemetry.

Open questions to resolve during pilot kickoff:
- Which model family to prioritize for cost/accuracy baseline?
- Is sample traffic representative of peak bursts or steady-state?
- Who is the single escalation contact for network changes?

Notes to self (facilitator):
- Keep demo scripts under 6 minutes each.
- Have one fallback recording for every live demo step.
- Use the Console token breakdown example to show concrete cost impact of batching.

End of doc.
